A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UPFI research, with matching central methods, theoretical results, and experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original bistable-system simulations, gene-regulatory-network experiments, and analyses of monocyte-neutrophil single-cell data, including results in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical studies and adds higher-dimensional simulations, flow-matching comparisons, runtime measurements, and regularization-ablation results.

M1.justification: The two-stage score-matching and weighted-characteristic algorithm is retained. Appendix C.2 introduces a limited loss adaptation for bistable experiments: the force regularization term is divided by dimension d, changing the penalty from lambda(||v||² + alpha|g|²) to lambda(d⁻¹||v||² + alpha|g|²).

E1.justification: The bistable simulations expand from dimensions 2, 5, and 10 to include 25 and 50, adding higher-dimensional input scenarios within the same synthetic task. The seven-gene bifurcating system, eleven-gene haematopoietic system, and biological lineage-tracing dataset are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds optimal transport flow matching (OTFM) and its unbalanced variant (UOTFM) alongside the retained PFI, fitness-ODE, TIGON++, and DeepRUOT comparators. These introduce a substantial additional comparison family on the existing bistable benchmark; Appendix C.6 and Figure 6 document their evaluation.

E3.justification: The reported bistable training settings change materially: the score-network learning rate for d ≤ 10 falls from 0.01 to 0.003, and regularization is revised. Tables 5–6 introduce 256-unit hidden layers and 100,000 score-training/25,000 dynamics-training iterations for d > 10. New flow-matching coupling settings and the regularization sweep further expand the protocol.

E4.justification: V3 adds a focused regularization ablation absent from v1. Table 8 and Appendix C.11 vary lambda and alpha on the ten-dimensional bistable system, measuring force-recovery error and growth-rate correlation to examine their tradeoff. Earlier noise-model and network-inference analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark estimates with ± spreads without specifying run/seed counts or explaining what those spreads represent. V3 extends this reporting style to runtimes but introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises existing bistable scores and adds higher-dimensional and flow-matching results. For example, UPFI's d = 10 path energy distance changes from 0.50 ± 0.23 to 0.05 ± 0.04 under revised training settings, so this is not a same-setting gain. Figure 3 is updated, and Tables 7–8 add runtime and ablation outcomes. Tables 2–4 retain identical results.

T1.justification: V3 corrects the density-evolution identity following Equation 4: the divergence term uses the probability-flow velocity u_t rather than the physical drift v_t. It also corrects the sign identifying net death. The central OU propositions, non-identifiability result, uniqueness theorem, and Appendix A–B proofs retain their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and Discussion retain the same principal contributions: UPFI separates drift, noise, and growth through a two-stage procedure, supports general noise models, and is evaluated on simulated and biological data. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: A new Scalability discussion explains computational costs, integration accuracy tradeoffs, and applicability to moderately high dimensions. Appendix C.11 adds an interpretation of the regularization ablation, hypothesizing implicit regularization from small networks and recommending little or no explicit regularization. Existing autonomy and frequency-only identifiability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds an explicit UPFI code-repository pointer, Euler-step guidance, dimension-specific training configurations, and implementation details for OTFM/UOTFM couplings and penalties. Table 7 newly reports runtimes. Together these substantially expand reproducibility information; the stated GPU and biological-data access instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds a dedicated Related work discussion positioning UPFI against static unbalanced transport, branching Schrödinger bridges, deterministic neural dynamics, coupled fitness models, and DeepRUOT. New references include proximal optimal transport, path-space mean-field Langevin inference, OTFM, and unbalanced neural maps. This expands substantive positioning beyond citation or bibliography edits.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact. V3 adds focused Related work and Scalability passages, expands Appendix C, swaps the fitness-ODE and TIGON++ subsection order, and makes local terminology, cross-reference, contact-information, and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: The comparative displays expand substantially: Table 1 gains comparator columns and dimension rows, Figure 3 is regenerated, and Figure 6 plus runtime and ablation Tables 7–8 are added. Tables 5–6 are restructured for dimension-dependent settings. Figures 1, 2, 4, and 5 retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the empirical claims easier to assess through relevant flow-matching comparisons, higher-dimensional tests, runtime measurements, and a regularization ablation. Code-access information and the corrected density identity also help. These gains are tempered by new reporting inconsistencies: Table 8 labels force error as similarity, and the weak-sensitivity interpretation overlooks growth correlation falling to 0.349 at lambda = alpha = 0.1. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
